title: fanoutqa: What were the regular season records of the Major League Baseball World Series winning teams in the last five years? (67fc04df63afb29c)

chat_history.content: What were the regular season records of the Major League Baseball World Series winning teams in the last five years?

content.content:
We need to provide regular season records of the World Series winning teams for last five years. That is 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019? Or maybe including 2018? "Last five years" from 2023 would be 2019-2023 inclusive. Provide the regular season records.

We need to get the records:

2023: MLB World Series champion was the Texas Rangers? Wait 2023 World Series winner was the Texas Rangers? Actually 2023 World Series champion was the Texas Rangers. Their regular season record was 92-70 (.562). Let’s confirm. Yes, Texas Rangers finished 92-70. Good.

2022: Los Angeles Dodgers won. Regular season record 106-56 (.656). They had a 106-56 record.

2021: Atlanta Braves won. Regular season record 101-61 (.623).

2020: Los Angeles Dodgers again. Regular season record 19-26 (.426). Actually 2020 season was shortened to 60 games. Dodgers finished 19-26 (.426).

2019: Washington Nationals won. Regular season record 87-75 (.537). Wait 2019 Nationals had 87-75. Yes.

Check 2024? Not needed. So answer: list each year with team and record.

We should confirm 2023 Texas Rangers record: They finished 92-70 (.562). Yes.

Check 2022 Dodgers: 106-56.

2021 Braves: 101-61.

2020 Dodgers: 19-26.

2019 Nationals: 87-75.

We might also mention that 2020 season was shortened due to COVID-19.

We should present in a table.

We should double-check 2019 Nationals: They actually finished 87-75, 1st in NL East. Yes.

Should we include 2018? Not needed.

Thus, answer accordingly.

content:
Here are the regular‑season records of the teams that won the MLB World Series over the last five completed seasons (2023 through 2019):

| Year | World Series Champion | Regular‑Season Record | Win % |
|------|-----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| **2023** | Texas Rangers | **92–70** | .562 |
| **2022** | Los Angeles Dodgers | **106–56** | .656 |
| **2021** | Atlanta Braves | **101–61** | .623 |
| **2020** | Los Angeles Dodgers | **19–26** | .426 *(60‑game season, COVID‑19 shortened)* |
| **2019** | Washington Nationals | **87–75** | .537 |

**Quick notes**

- **2020** was the only year in this span with a shortened 60‑game schedule due to the COVID‑19 pandemic, which explains the lower win total and the lower winning percentage for the Dodgers.
- All other seasons were the standard 162‑game schedule.
- The records shown are the final regular‑season win–loss totals that each team achieved before advancing to the postseason.
